title: Brent Crude Tops $100/Barrel for First Time Since July as US-Iran Tanker Strikes Escalate
detail: Brent crude futures rose 2.57% to $100.44/bbl on Wednesday — the first time above $100 since July — after CENTCOM's destruction of five Iranian tankers and Iran's retaliatory missile barrage on Jordan's Al-Azraq Air Base stoked fresh fears of a broader Strait of Hormuz supply disruption. TradingEconomics recorded the price as high as ~$100.76-102/bbl intraday. Goldman Sachs said intensifying shipping attacks were raising the probability of Brent exceeding $120/bbl. The jump extends a week-long climb driven by the tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes and continued Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

title: IAEA Board Refers Iran to UN Security Council for First Time in 20 Years
detail: The IAEA's 35-nation Board of Governors passed a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for breaching its non-proliferation obligations — the first such referral in two decades — with 23 in favor, Russia, China, and Niger against, and the remainder abstaining. The resolution directs IAEA chief Rafael Grossi to transmit the resolution, prior board decisions, and his latest report to the Security Council and General Assembly, and calls on Iran to provide information and inspector access to sites bombed by Israel and the US since the war began. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi condemned the move as based on 'fabrications,' writing on X that Western states 'attack Iran's nuclear facilities under safeguards, disrupt the normal verification process, and then use that very disruption as a pretext to issue a resolution.' Practical UN Security Council punitive measures remain unlikely since Iran's allies Russia and China hold veto power.

title: IRGC Claims Largest Shipping Attack Wave of the War — 10 Vessels Targeted; Seafarer Killed, One Missing Off Dubai
detail: Iran's IRGC said it targeted 10 vessels in the Strait of Hormuz region on Sept 9 — two US Navy ships (both attempts failed, per CENTCOM) and eight commercial tankers — in what analysts described as the largest declared wave of shipping attacks by either side since the war began. UKMTO reported several merchant vessels struck by disabling fire overnight in the northern Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. The Gibraltar-flagged oil products tanker Hercules Star was hit at anchorage roughly 24 nautical miles off Dubai's Port Rashid; charterer Peninsula confirmed one seafarer killed and a second missing, with maritime security sources saying the vessel may have been struck by a drone (unconfirmed, and Peninsula has not confirmed a cause). Separately, the Panama-flagged, Greek-owned tanker New Andros, carrying about 2 million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil under charter to the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company, caught fire after a drone strike in Iraqi territorial waters near Al-Faw at approximately 0600 local time; Iraq's oil ministry reported only minor hull damage and no injuries among the 22 crew. No group claimed the Hercules Star or New Andros attacks specifically. CENTCOM said no US vessel was struck and that 'all IRGC attempted attacks failed.'

media.caption: The Gibraltar-flagged tanker Hercules Star, struck at anchorage off Dubai's Port Rashid, Sept 9, 2026

confidenceReason: The Hercules Star casualty is confirmed on the record by charterer Peninsula and corroborated by multiple outlets; the IRGC's broad 10-vessel claim is partially corroborated by UKMTO's overnight incident reports, but the attacker for the Hercules Star and New Andros incidents specifically is unclaimed/unconfirmed, and CENTCOM disputes any successful strike on US vessels.
